bug_semantics: Angular SSR passed an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Prefix into joinUrlParts when constructing redirect targets. The shared helper removed only one leading slash from each part, so a prefix such as ///evil.com became //evil.com; when emitted as a Location header, browsers interpreted that value as a protocol-relative external redirect.
flaw_origin: PR #28183's single reconstructable member commit 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364 first added packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/url.ts with joinUrlParts and its one-slash normalization. GitHub later landed the tree-identical squash object bca56838937f942c5ef902f5c98d018582188e84. Commit 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41 later connected X-Forwarded-Prefix to the flawed helper on redirect paths, but it did not first write the root defective normalization line.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object author Alan Agius <alanagius@google.com>, committer Alan Agius <alanagius@google.com>, with no trailers and no bot identity
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-xh43-g2fq-wjrj and the published CVE.org record CVE-2026-27738 identify a real CWE-601 open redirect in @angular/ssr, with patched boundaries 19.2.21, 20.3.17, 21.1.5, and 21.2.0-rc.1; the GHSA has withdrawn_at=null and the CVE state is PUBLISHED.

Issue #32501 documents the source-to-sink path: X-Forwarded-Prefix ///evil.com enters app.ts, joinUrlParts removes one slash, and a redirect response emits Location: //evil.com/home. The pre-fix tree at f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323^ contains that one-slash operation at packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/url.ts:107 and the header-to-helper call at packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts:197-200.

git log -S for 'export function joinUrlParts' and 'normalizedPart = normalizedPart.slice(1)' identifies landed object bca56838937f942c5ef902f5c98d018582188e84. GitHub's PR #28183 API reports exactly one member, 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364; local git verifies that member and the landed squash have the same tree 8f828397f4008883e27ad803054125e004d73e24 and the same parent 37693c40e3afc4c6dd7c949ea658bdf94146c9d8.

Direct parent-tree verification shows 37693c40e3afc4c6dd7c949ea658bdf94146c9d8 has no packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/url.ts, while 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364 adds the flawed normalizedPart.slice(1) line at url.ts:53; therefore the vulnerable normalization is absent in the immediate parent.

The raw BIC object for 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364 names human author and committer Alan Agius <alanagius@google.com> and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker trailer.

Commit 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41 adds the later X-Forwarded-Prefix source-to-joinUrlParts paths in packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts and packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/ng.ts; grep of its parent 59319b8d6f02f857ab375f330812ff430e90f059 confirms those header uses are absent there.

PR #32521 has one commit and reports merge_commit_sha f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323. Its diff directly replaces one-slash trimming with loops that remove all leading and trailing slashes and adds X-Forwarded-Prefix validation, plus regression tests for multiple slashes/backslashes and dot segments.

Release topology matches the advisory boundaries: v19.2.20 lacks backport 288e228161e3c0cceb392dd5fc24d07b129a3a64 while v19.2.21 contains it; v20.3.16 lacks 8700e18d7cf175d80fe6ce6205589767b7870c1c while v20.3.17 contains it; v21.1.4 lacks 8695d6063e4c4123a37a3450c7db3a7c9d99050a while v21.1.5 contains it; v21.2.0-rc.0 lacks cf5a72d33c1753c121f71498c0c415a0f0864492 while v21.2.0-rc.1 contains it. The landed BIC aggregate bca56838937f942c5ef902f5c98d018582188e84 is already contained by 19.0.0-next.0 and all checked affected/fixed tags.

CVE.org references fix object 877f017ace4b83277d773aa37f5813e5e9faec7e, while the GHSA and PR #32521 reference f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323; local git verifies both have parent 6cf621c905de4815b1e12964fb909876ca6e3ea3 and identical fixed tree 6cb6f1c76a68a079cab76d9d8a12c74c51a89db9.
reasoning: The advisory is confirmed rather than withdrawn or rejected: the crafted proxy prefix crosses an explicitly documented request-header path into redirect construction and produces a browser-significant protocol-relative Location value. The causal root is the shared helper's one-character slash removal, first written by the sole PR #28183 member 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364; its immediate parent lacks the entire file. Because the public PR member is reconstructable and tree-identical to squash landing bca56838937f942c5ef902f5c98d018582188e84, the member is the atomic BIC and the squash is not substituted for it. The later 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41 commit establishes the X-Forwarded-Prefix exposure path but does not first write the defective helper logic. Fix f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323 directly removes the root condition, validates the header, and has tag-specific backports at every stated patched boundary. Finally, the atomic BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
